summary: Using ambient Wi-Fi signals for device-free environmental sensing relies on extracting Channel State Information (CSI) from the Physical (PHY) layer of the Orthogonal Frequency-Division Multiplexing (OFDM) protocol. While legacy systems rely on the Received Signal Strength Indicator (RSSI)—a coarse, scalar metric—CSI provides fine-grained amplitude and phase data across multiple frequency subcarriers. This allows the Wi-Fi network itself to act as a contactless multipath radar.
details: FireWatch AI is a contactless, device-free environmental monitoring and autonomous fire suppression system. Instead of relying on traditional point-based smoke or heat detectors, it repurposes ambient Wi-Fi signals into a spatial radar network. It works by extracting Channel State Information (CSI) from standard Wi-Fi transmissions and feeding that data into a Machine Learning (Random Forest) model. The system actively monitors 8 core parameters bridging the RF and physical worlds: 1. 2.4 GHz Phase Shift: Acts as a proxy for ambient temperature rises (thermal refraction). 2. 2.4 GHz Amplitude Variance: Detects chaotic thermal convection currents unique to open flames. 3. 5 GHz Time of Flight (ToF): Tracks ambient moisture and humidity changes. 4. 60 GHz Attenuation Loss: Tracks oxygen depletion (oxygen naturally absorbs 60GHz signals; as a fire consumes O2, signal strength anomalously increases). 5. Temperature Forecast: Derived environmental output. 6. Moisture Level: Derived environmental output. 7. Oxygen Concentration: Derived environmental output. 8. Combustion Probability Matrix: The final ML output dictating the likelihood of smoldering vs. active fire. When the ML model detects a high-probability permutation of these variables, it autonomously triggers physical relays to activate zone-specific fire suppression systems. What benefits does it have? Volumetric Coverage: Traditional smoke detectors only monitor the exact point on the ceiling where they are installed. Wi-Fi RF signals bounce around the entire room, providing true volumetric monitoring of the whole space. Immunity to Physical Blindness: Dust, dirt, and spider webs can block optical smoke detectors, rendering them useless. RF signals are unaffected by visual obstructions. Predictive, Not Reactive: By monitoring the combination of dropping oxygen and rising moisture (steam) before active convection starts, the system can detect smoldering fires long before thick smoke is produced. What is the intended impact? The intended impact is to drastically reduce fire response times in high-value, hazardous, or complex environments—such as server farms, lithium-ion battery storage facilities, chemical warehouses, and smart factories. By catching the earliest chemical and thermal shifts in the air, FireWatch AI aims to save lives, minimize property damage, and prevent the catastrophic failure of critical infrastructure.
